A2.text:
Tural works with computers in Baku. His grandmother, Sevinj, makes beautiful carpets in Icherisheher. Her carpets are popular with tourists. Tural wanted to help her business.

Last month, he bought her a tablet. “This is very modern, nənə,” Tural said. “You can save your carpet pictures here. We will use a strong password for your cybersecurity.”

Sevinj smiled and poured him tea. She looked at the shiny tablet, but she kept her old paper notebook on the desk.

One Saturday, Tural visited her shop. He wanted to show her a software update. He clicked a button, but suddenly the tablet had a crash. The screen went completely black.

Tural panicked. “Oh no! We lost all your new customer orders. I must pull the plug and take this to a repair shop,” he said.

Sevinj laughed softly. “Do not worry, my boy,” she said.

She opened a small drawer and took out her paper notebook. “I wrote all the orders here this morning,” she explained. “Computers are fast, but paper does not need electricity.”

Tural looked at the notebook. He felt a little silly, but he was very happy.

“You are right, nənə,” he smiled. “Sometimes the old way is the best.”

B1.text:
Tural was a software engineer in Baku. His grandmother, Sevinj, ran a small traditional carpet shop in Icherisheher. Tourists loved her colourful designs, but her business methods were extremely old-fashioned. She kept all her customer records in a heavy notebook.

Tural decided it was time to modernize her shop. He bought her a high-tech tablet and set up cloud storage so she would never lose her designs.

“This is a cutting edge system, nənə,” Tural explained, showing her the screen. “Everything is saved online now. We just need to create a secure password for good cybersecurity.”

Sevinj smiled, gave him a slice of pakhlava, and nodded. However, Tural noticed she still kept her trusty paper notebook next to the cash register.

A few weeks later, Tural came to the shop on a busy Saturday afternoon. He noticed a notification for a system update and quickly tapped the screen to install it. Suddenly, the tablet froze, made a strange noise, and suffered a complete crash.

Tural panicked. He tried to restart it, but nothing happened. “This is terrible! We might lose the new orders,” he groaned. “I need to pull the plug, take this home, and fix the whole system.”

“Relax, my dear,” Sevinj said calmly. She opened her laptop, typed something quickly, and the tablet screen suddenly lit up again.

Tural stared at her in shock. “How did you do that?”

“I read about this problem online yesterday,” she laughed. “I also used an Artificial Intelligence program to translate the manual into Azerbaijani. You need to get up to speed, Tural! I am not just drinking tea all day.”

Tural could not stop laughing. His grandmother was much smarter than he realized.

B2.text:
Tural, a young software developer based in Baku, was determined to bring his grandmother’s business into the twenty-first century. Sevinj ran a charming, traditional carpet boutique in the heart of Icherisheher. While tourists adored her intricate, hand-woven designs, Tural was horrified by her archaic administrative methods. She managed her entire inventory using a fading leather notebook and a jar of ink.

Hoping to revolutionize her daily operations, Tural gifted her a premium tablet. He proudly set up remote cloud storage and introduced a smart algorithm designed to track her most popular carpet patterns.

“This is truly cutting edge technology, nənə,” Tural declared, tapping the sleek screen. “It features full automation for your customer receipts. We just need to establish a complex password to ensure top-tier cybersecurity.”

Sevinj offered a warm, tolerant smile, poured him a glass of pear compote, and nodded politely. Yet, whenever Tural visited, he noticed that the leather notebook never left its prime position on the wooden counter.

A month later, Tural dropped by during the chaotic Novruz holiday rush. Seeing a pending software update notification on the tablet, he absentmindedly initiated the installation. Almost instantly, the device froze, emitted a sharp beep, and experienced a catastrophic crash. The screen went entirely black.

Tural’s face went pale. He frantically tapped the glass. “Oh no, the operating system is corrupted! We’ve lost all the holiday orders,” he panicked. “I’ll have to pull the plug on this device and take it to a specialist immediately.”

“Sit down and drink your compote,” Sevinj instructed calmly. She reached under the counter, pulled out her own modern laptop, and swiftly typed a command into a terminal window. Within seconds, the tablet rebooted, displaying the orders perfectly intact.

Tural’s jaw dropped. “How on earth did you manage that?”

“I was curious about your system,” she chuckled, her eyes sparkling with amusement. “So, I used Artificial Intelligence to study the code and learned how to reboot the server. You really need to get up to speed, my boy. Did you honestly think I survived in business for forty years without learning how to adapt?”

Tural leaned back, shaking his head in sheer admiration.
